correctness.rationale: Every factor of Q_T is prime to a, and the chosen b_T is also prime to a. In Q_T=ax+b_T y the congruence forces y≡−1 mod a and the size constraint gives 2≤y≤T. For composite y use its least prime divisor at most √T; for prime y use the −1 residue-class factor. In either case p divides Q_T and y but not a, so divides x, including when x=0. Consequently Q_T is not primitively representable. The fixed-modulus prime number theorem gives log Q_T=T/φ(a)+o(T); the additional small-prime weight is O(√T log T). The offset of b_T from Q_T/T is less than a, yielding b_T→∞ and Q_T/(b_T log b_T)→φ(a). Every cover must include every prime in the forced class because that prime itself is an eligible y. The matching log-weight upper bound from Q_T gives asymptotic optimality only in the stated cover class. An independent exact check gives Q_20=1870, b_20=95 and y=2,5,8,11,14,17 with respective gcds 2,5,2,11,2,17 for a=3; it does not compute the exact Frobenius number or reproduce all 615 cases. The supplied script was inspected, not executed.
